title: Will They Talk: Offered and Requested Quality of Service, and the Silence When They Do Not Match

questions.question: A camera driver publishes best effort and a node subscribes with the default profile, reliable. What happens?
options: They are never connected, nothing is delivered, and the only report is a warning in a log: the most common cause of a subscriber that gets no data
questions.explanation: The middleware cannot give reliable delivery from a publisher that sends once.

questions.question: Is the compatibility rule symmetric?
options: No: a reliable offer meets either request and a best effort offer only best effort, so the order of offer and request matters
questions.explanation: Strength has an order and the offer must be at least the request.

questions.question: An offer of a message every 0.5 s meets which request?
options: One for every 0.5 s or longer, or no deadline at all, but not every 0.1 s
questions.explanation: A faster promise meets a slower demand.

questions.question: A subscriber requests a deadline and the publisher offers none. Compatible?
options: No: silence is not a promise, so a demand cannot be met by offering nothing
questions.explanation: A request of no deadline is met by anything.

questions.question: Why does the check name each property that does not fit?
options: A yes or no leaves a person guessing which of five properties differed: the camera against the demanding node gave three named reasons
questions.explanation: A person fixing it knows what to change.

questions.question: What did the matcher do with the detector, subscribing with the default profile to the camera's image?
options: Did not connect it and reported one reason, reliability, while the best effort viewer was connected
questions.explanation: Three links and one mismatch in the test.
